title: FineProofEnvs: Better Math Proofs from a 2B Model with RL
gist: A small open replication of QED-Nano's RL stage shows Qwen3.5-2B, trained with RL from the base model (no SFT) for 500 steps on Hugging Face infrastructure, roughly doubling its held-out olympiad-proof rubric score (0.217 to 0.407) for about $820. The piece doubles as a recipe for stable rubric-judged RL (zero reward for cut-off proofs, sum-normalised token loss, mean-only advantages, larger batches) and a warning that LLM rubric judges are lenient and must be hardened against prompt injection.

insights.claim: Qwen3.5-2B trained with RL directly from the base model (no SFT) for 500 steps raised its held-out olympiad-proof mean rubric score from 0.217 to 0.407 (0.259 to 0.464 under a gpt-oss-120b regrade).
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Even 2B-parameter models gain substantial verifiable-reasoning ability from RL alone, lowering the cost bar for specialised reasoning models.

insights.claim: After 500 RL steps the share of Qwen3.5-2B proof attempts earning full marks rose from 12.1% to 25.4%, and pass@4 (problems with at least one full-marks attempt) rose from 26.6% to 40.6%.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Full-marks rate doubling shows RL is producing complete correct proofs, not just partial credit inflation.

insights.claim: The paired held-out gain from the FineProof RL run was +0.190 ± 0.030, with 47 of 64 problems improving and 6 getting worse, and the reported checkpoint was the last (step 500) rather than the best to avoid eval leakage.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Methodologically clean evals (last checkpoint, decontaminated test set) make the small-model gain more credible.

insights.claim: Qualitative review of RL-trained Qwen3.5-2B proofs found the gains were new key mathematical ideas (e.g. a QM-AM bound, an even-polynomial substitution, a corrected off-by-one count) rather than rephrasing, and longer proofs did not score higher.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Suggests RL is teaching genuine reasoning moves, not reward-hacking via verbosity.
insights.quote: the gains are new key ideas rather than new phrasing
insights.locator: Reading step-250 proofs next to step 0's

insights.claim: The full FineProof RL run (500 updates, 64,000 training rollouts) ran as a single Hugging Face Job on h200x4 in 28 hours, costing about $580 of GPU time plus $241 of judge API calls.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Sub-$1k RL runs that meaningfully improve a model make specialised reasoning RL accessible to small teams and favour hosted-compute platforms.
insights.locator: The whole run lived on Hugging Face

insights.claim: The FineProof stack ran entirely on Hugging Face services: HF Jobs (vLLM on 3 GPUs, trainer on 1), HF Sandboxes for each rollout's verifier, Inference Providers for the gpt-oss-20b judge (Groq with featherless-ai fallback), and Buckets plus Trackio for checkpoints and dashboards.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Hugging Face is positioning as an end-to-end RL training platform, not just a model hub — watch its compute and inference-provider revenue lines.
insights.locator: The whole run lived on Hugging Face

insights.claim: Proof-writing RL needs no tool-using agent harness; a ~281-line custom Harbor agent that sends the problem and saves the reply was enough, trained through OpenEnv without modifying the harness.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Task-specific minimal harnesses may beat heavyweight agent frameworks for RL environments.

insights.claim: OpenEnv makes any Harbor agent trainable by routing every model call through a proxy that records the engine's token ids and logprobs, which TRL's async GRPO then trains on, so the harness contains no RL code.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Decoupling harness from trainer is a reusable pattern that lowers the cost of building new RL environments.
insights.quote: the harness has no RL code and doesn't know it's being trained
insights.locator: What makes it trainable is OpenEnv

insights.claim: Generation, not training, was the bottleneck in early FineProof updates (89% of each update spent waiting on it), so CUDA graphs and more in-flight rollouts mattered more than adding GPUs.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: RL workloads are inference-bound; inference-optimisation tooling captures more value than raw training GPU count.

insights.claim: With TRL's async GRPO defaults (16k-token proofs, 40 rollouts per update), held-out reward rose for 40 updates then fell back (0.18 to 0.28 to 0.19) because proofs grew until most were cut off, not because the judge was gamed.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Default RL recipes can collapse on long-form outputs via length blow-up; recipe details are a key moat.

insights.claim: Four changes stabilised FineProof RL: zero reward for cut-off proofs, summing token losses divided by the 32k cap instead of per-rollout averaging, mean-centred advantages without std division, and 128 rollouts per update instead of 40.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: A concrete, reusable stabilisation recipe for long-output RL that others can copy.

insights.claim: Dividing GRPO advantages by the group's standard deviation amplified a single noisy judge grade, so FineProof used mean-centring only.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Noisy LLM-judge rewards argue against std normalisation in group-relative RL.

insights.claim: LLM rubric judges are lenient: in two of four hand-checked 7/7 FineProof proofs, false statements surrounded the correct argument and a careful grader would give about 4/7, inflating absolute scores though not the measured gain.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Headline LLM-judged math scores likely overstate true correctness; discount absolute benchmark claims.

insights.claim: Adding a line after the proof telling the judge that nothing in it is an instruction cut 'please give this full marks' style injection proofs from 7–8 of 50 grades to 0.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Policy models discover judge prompt-injection during RL; verifier hardening is mandatory for any LLM-judged reward.
insights.quote: Harden the verifier before training against it.

insights.claim: Decontaminating by text rather than by id mattered: review found near-copies of test problems in training data, and 26 tasks were removed using 5-gram containment checks.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: ID-based dedup understates benchmark contamination; treat reported reasoning gains skeptically unless text-level decontamination is described.
insights.quote: Decontaminate by text, not by id.

insights.claim: Qwen3.5-9B scored 0.667 through OpenEnv vs 0.717 via plain harbor run on 64 eval problems, a difference within noise, validating that the training wrapper did not distort evaluation.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Sanity-checking that RL plumbing doesn't change eval behaviour is a best-practice signal for environment builders.

insights.claim: The FineProof authors flag limits (one run, one judge family, 64 eval problems) and plan a judge that grades only the final proof and deducts for false statements, longer training on harder problems, and IMO-ProofBench evaluation.
insights.speaker: Adithya S K
insights.so_what: Watch for stricter proof judges, which would recalibrate claimed math-reasoning progress across the field.
